rows.title: Soil Fertility

text_1.eng: Soil fertility is how healthy and rich the soil is for growing plants.

text_2.eng: It means the soil has enough nutrients, water, and good structure to help plants grow well.

rows.title: Soil Erosion

text_1.eng: Soil erosion is the process where the top layer of soil is washed away by wind, water, or human activity.

text_2.eng: It makes the soil less fertile and harder for plants to grow.

rows.title: Agroecology

text_1.eng: Agroecology is just farming in a way that works with nature.

text_2.eng: It helps keep your soil healthy and your farm strong. Here’s how:

rows.text_1: Agroecology is just farming in a way that works with nature.

rows.title: Diversity

media_transcript.eng:
Plant different crops and keep different varieties of animals. Some plants grow fast, some slow this way, if one fails, others still give you food and income. 
You can also harvest more than once in a season and have a balanced diet for your family.
helps with pest control too"

rows.title: Crop rotation

media_transcript.eng: Don’t plant the same crop in the same spot every year. Some crops take a lot of nutrients from the soil, others give back. Rotating them keeps the soil rich and prevents it from getting tired.

rows.media_transcript: Don’t plant the same crop in the same spot every year. Some crops take a lot of nutrients from the soil, others give back. Rotating them keeps the soil rich and prevents it from getting tired.

rows.title: Resilience

media_transcript.eng: Choose crops and animals that survive well in your area. Some crops and animals can handle dry spells, others wet conditions. This way, your farm can recover from tough weather.

rows.title: Bokashi

media_transcript.eng: Bokashi is a type of organic manure that’s faster to make than regular compost. It is partially fermented before use, and decomposition continues even after you apply it to the soil.

rows.media_transcript: Bokashi is a type of organic manure that’s faster to make than regular compost. It is partially fermented before use, and decomposition continues even after you apply it to the soil.

rows.title: Boma Compost

media_transcript.eng:
Boma Compost is made by placing farm residues in a livestock shed to absorb animal urine, which is rich in nitrogen. After some time, the mixture is collected and applied to the farm.
It should always be prepared and kept under shade to prevent nutrient loss from direct sunlight.

rows.title: Garden Compost

media_transcript.eng:
Garden compost is an organic fertilizer made by decomposing crop residues under shade until they become a rich, soil-like material.

When collecting materials, it is important to choose those that add nutrients to the soil—especially nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium —to ensure the compost supports healthy plant growth. Time taken for compost to be ready depends on:  The size of the pile, the materials used, and the moisture content.
Smaller piles generally take longer to decompose.

rows.title: Green Manure

media_transcript.eng:
Green manure involves planting leguminous crops like beans, soya, or lablab, letting them grow until about half flowering, then cutting them down before planting the main crop.

Lablab is especially recommended because it acts as a cover crop, and its seeds are both nutritious and valuable.
